classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b scaffold the work: the angle-sum subtraction is routine, and the student then reads off which angle is opposite the 5 cm side in each triangle. The hardest demand is part c. The student must see that equal angle sets are not enough, and that AAS needs the equal side opposite corresponding angles. Here 5 cm is opposite 75° in one triangle and 45° in the other. They then have to put this into a written explanation. This is more than the direct test-naming in p11-q3, which has no scaffolding steps or written justification. It is a little less than p15-q12, which needs a non-signposted reason for congruence followed by a consequence. It is also well below p13-q6, which asks for the same decision with less scaffolding.
